name: Gerald Ford
role: President of the United States (1974–1977); House Minority Leader; Republican member of Congress from Michigan (1949–1973)
summary: A Midwestern Republican who stressed fiscal restraint, vetoes of spending bills, deregulation and returning decisions to states and localities, while accepting Social Security, Medicare and a modest safety net. In foreign policy he continued detente with the Soviet Union and China, kept a strong defense and alliances, and backed the ERA and a state-by-state approach to abortion. After office he drew attention for supporting equal treatment for gay couples.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Told Congress in 1976 that the country could not realistically afford federally dictated national health insurance covering all 215 million Americans; proposed catastrophic coverage and a consolidated state grant instead.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called massive government regulation a 'petty tyranny' on the economy, pushed deregulation of airlines, trucking and railroads, and said jobs come from private business, not government.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Preferred broad tax cuts for middle-income taxpayers and opposed Carter's platform spending; his one proposal aimed at upper incomes was a temporary 5 percent surcharge in 1974, which he withdrew weeks later. In 1976 he accepted a higher minimum tax on the wealthy only as part of a tax bill he found imperfect.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Wanted less regulation overall and vetoed strip-mining and auto-emission measures, while pledging stricter antitrust enforcement; the net direction was fewer rules.

cut-welfare.rationale: Said many welfare programs were inequitable and invited abuse and asked for tighter eligibility and food stamp reform, but also refused to dump welfare on the states and kept support for the truly needy.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Backed legislation letting the attorney general obtain wiretaps in security cases and said a crippled intelligence service endangered the country.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Directed stepped-up enforcement against hard drugs and urged mandatory fixed sentences for hard-drug dealing; his statements concerned hard drugs, not all recreational use.

state-harmful.rationale: Described government as existing to create and preserve conditions for people to succeed and called for 'sound, active government'.

limit-guns.rationale: Rejected registration of handguns or their owners as ineffective and said the answer was not to take guns away from law-abiding citizens but to jail criminals who use them.

empower-police-military.rationale: Proposed about $7 billion over five years for state and local law enforcement, extra federal agents, prosecutors and prisons, and real growth in the defense budget.

decide-locally.rationale: Pushed revenue sharing, block grants and consolidation of 59 federal programs to 'do the job closer to home', and urged returning decisions to state and local officials.

rehabilitation.rationale: Argued criminals must be put in prison so they cannot harm others and that punishment must be swift and certain; he stressed incapacitation and sentencing, not rehabilitation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: In 2001 said gay and lesbian couples 'ought to be treated equally. Period.'; reported by Wikipedia from a news interview, and it is unclear whether he meant marriage specifically.

abortion-legal.rationale: As president backed a federal constitutional amendment letting each state decide and opposed Roe v. Wade; later in life he was described as identifying as pro-choice and urged the GOP to drop the issue. Evidence points both ways.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said a constitutional amendment allowing voluntary prayer in public schools had merit and that he would favor it.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Pointed to enforcement of the Voting Rights Act, housing and anti-redlining law, and minority business programs as administration policy.

free-trade.rationale: Reported that his administration made progress in trade negotiations and avoided protectionism during the recession.

nation-first.rationale: Said that in a global, interdependent economy relations with other nations 'become more, not less, important' and that nations must work together.

limit-growth.rationale: Sought sustained economic growth, vetoed a strip-mining bill over jobs and coal supply, and favored easing auto emission standards.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Called for expediting clean and safe nuclear power production and expanding nuclear generation as part of his energy program.

central-planning.rationale: Opposed wage and price controls and said controls never really stop inflation; his program relied on voluntary action and market incentives.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Proposed estate tax changes so family farms and businesses could be passed on without being sold to pay taxes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Counted avoiding protectionism during the recession as an achievement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Proposed an energy independence authority to finance vital energy investment, but otherwise relied on private investment and tax incentives.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Asked that family farms and family-owned small businesses be preserved because they strengthen America and the economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Praised an independent Federal Reserve and its responsible monetary policy; he never spoke to abolition, but backed the institution.

one-party-rule.rationale: Praised the American system in which the opposition party 'doesn't go underground' but keeps functioning vigorously in Congress, and said the people choose leaders freely.

democracy-best.rationale: Described free elections as the foundation of the republic and accepted his own defeat in 1976 with a smooth transfer of power.

separate-church-state.rationale: Favored a voluntary school-prayer amendment and publicly asked for prayer, though he did not argue for establishing religion.

military-superiority.rationale: Said American military power is 'without equal' and he intended to keep it so, and that the country must never be second in defense.

limit-population.rationale: Adopted NSDM 314 as policy and said US leadership was essential to combat population growth (as reported by Wikipedia).

collective-farming.rationale: Praised American farmers for what they produce free of government control and sought to preserve the family farm.

taxation-theft.rationale: Treated taxation as a legitimate means of financing government, asking Congress for temporary tax surcharges and increased payroll taxes to protect Social Security.

total-state.rationale: Called a federal police force repugnant, sought to curb government intrusion into individual lives and wanted more individual freedom and self-reliance.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Declared his administration 'dedicated to the survival and security of Israel' and cited arms sales and aid to it.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Vetoed an emergency jobs bill as 'too much stimulus, too late' and several appropriations because of deficits.

national-self-determination.rationale: Said Poland, Yugoslavia and Romania are independent and autonomous and that Africa should shape its own future free of outside intervention.

force-without-un.rationale: Ordered Marines to rescue the Mayaguez crew in 1975 on his own authority, with no UN approval reported.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Said he would 'do what is right as God gives me to see the right' and that the laws of God govern consciences; he cited prayer and a higher Power as guides.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Was an outspoken supporter of the Equal Rights Amendment and proclaimed that 'all men and all women are equal before the law' (as quoted by Wikipedia).

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Described his Justice Department as enforcing the Voting Rights Act and housing and anti-redlining laws.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Proposed more domestic oil, gas and coal production, natural gas deregulation and doubling coal output by 1985.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Backed federal programs for health care for the elderly and poor, Social Security, housing aid and revenue sharing, far beyond defense and justice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Proclaimed that all men and all women are equal before the law in backing the ERA (as quoted by Wikipedia).

consent-of-governed.rationale: Said in 1974 that the people rule under the Constitution and that his authority rested on confirmation by their prayers and their elected representatives.

separated-powers.rationale: Defended checks and balances, saying a Republican president should check a Democratic Congress, and described three independent branches reserving sovereignty to the people.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Rejected compulsory wage and price controls, saying they never really stop inflation.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Told Congress 'there can be only one Commander in Chief' while acknowledging its war and spending powers.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Said alliances with Atlantic democracies and Japan had never been more solid and called NATO the cornerstone of American defense policy.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Urged the Trident, B-1 and a new ICBM and said the US could never tolerate a shift in the strategic balance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Said the Federal Reserve chairman 'should be independent' and that making him a tool of the governing party would be catastrophic.

collective-defense.rationale: Called NATO's security the cornerstone of US defense policy and launched a program to deter or defeat aggression in Europe.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Told Congress that public officials bring 'no hereditary status or gift of infallibility'.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Said 'our great Republic is a government of laws and not of men' and 'the law is no respecter of persons'.

ban-cartels.rationale: Pledged vigorous antitrust enforcement against price fixing and bid rigging and asked for much higher penalties.

no-bailouts.rationale: In October 1975 said he would veto any federal bailout of New York City but within weeks backed conditional federal loans; contested.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Supported trade negotiations, opposed protectionism and said a global economy made relations with other nations more important.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Cited enforcement of laws against discrimination in housing, credit and employment as administration policy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Praised the orderly succession of freely elected presidents and Congresses.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Called Social Security a vital part of the economic system whose value is no longer debatable and proposed higher payroll taxes to protect its trust fund.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Said Congress's power of the purse is ample authority that should be jealously guarded.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Backed CIA aid to the FNLA and UNITA in Angola and criticized Congress for cutting it off.

job-guarantee.rationale: Vetoed an emergency public service jobs bill and called make-work temporary jobs dead end.

non-intervention.rationale: Sought to help friendly forces in Angola and sent Marines to the Mayaguez; he rejected a rule against intervening abroad.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Vetoed Freedom of Information Act amendments citing military secrets and law enforcement, while stating support for the direction of the legislation; Congress overrode the veto.

defeat-communism.rationale: Rejected a return to Cold War relations, saying the US should negotiate with the Soviet Union from strength; he pursued detente and SALT.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred: in 2001 said gay and lesbian couples should be treated equally and wanted a federal ban on anti-gay job discrimination, which is incompatible with criminalization.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Held up the free functioning of the opposition party as the mark of the American system.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Called his office a trust from the people and said sovereignty is reserved to the people, while acknowledging a higher Power.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Raised defense spending and said America must never be second in defense.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Led NATO alliance commitments and said alliance cooperation had never been closer.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Said government should be of laws and not of men and that the law is no respecter of persons.

racial-franchise.rationale: Said his Justice Department was fully enforcing the Voting Rights Act.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Called for more prisons, prosecutors, marshals and police support.

arms-reduction.rationale: Negotiated the Vladivostok limits on strategic launchers while insisting on strong defenses.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Repeatedly asked Congress to approve a ceiling on federal spending and set a target limit for the budget.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Maintained and modernized the US strategic arsenal while negotiating a SALT limit rather than disarming.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Proposed mandatory sentences for crimes with guns and for hard drug sales and 'mandatory certain prison sentences'.

women-suffrage.rationale: Supported the ERA and proclaimed men and women equal before the law; appointed women to Cabinet posts.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Asked that food stamps go only to those most in need and Medicare changes target older people and the poor.

notes: Pardon of Nixon (1974), clemency program (1974) and Mayaguez rescue (1975) are recorded but map to few statements. His 1974 tax-surcharge proposal was dropped in favor of tax cuts; he reversed on NYC aid within weeks. Betty Ford's views were not used. Helsinki Final Act speech text and the NYC speech text could not be opened; only arrival remarks and a reference page were used.
